questions.text: Explain the impacts of geographical explorations.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the impacts of geographical explorations. (D)

answer.value:
Impact of Geographical Discoveries:
The Earth was recognized as round and vast.
Trade Monopoly Competition: European nations competed to establish colonies in newly discovered lands, intensifying trade rivalries in America, Africa, and Asia.
Wealth Accumulation: Colonies supplied raw materials, enriching European nations.
Capitalism and Industrial Revolution: European countries' wealth fueled capitalism and sparked the Industrial Revolution.

questions.text: Describe the role of Martin Luther in the Reformation movement.
questions.text_as_printed: Describe the role of Martin Luther in the Reformation movement. (A)

answer.value:
Martin Luther and Protestantism:
Martin Luther rejected Catholic Church doctrines and opposed the sale of indulgences in 1517.
The Catholic Church believed the Pope had the power to reduce sinners' punishment, granted through Christ's and missionaries' good deeds.
Luther fiercely opposed indulgence sales.
His followers were called Protestants, comprising half of Germany's population.
The Thirty Years' War resulted from Catholic-Protestant conflicts

questions.text: What are the causes for the Industrial Revolution?
questions.text_as_printed: What are the causes for the Industrial Revolution? (D)

answer.value:
Causes of Industrial Revolution:
Renaissance-inspired scientific inventions led to machine production.
Colonies increased trade and demand for finished goods.

questions.text: Explain the causes for Reformation.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the causes for Reformation. (A)

answer.value:
Causes of Reformation:
Religious Causes: Corruption and immorality in the Roman Catholic Church, with Popes and clergy living luxuriously (e.g., Pope Alexander VI had 11 wives and 6 children). Sale of indulgences to fund St. Peter's Church was opposed by Martin Luther, Boccaccio, Erasmus, and John Wycliffe.
Political Causes: Medieval conflicts between emperors and Popes hurt imperial pride.
Rise of Nationalism: Nations like England, Spain, France, and Portugal resented Church interference.
Renaissance Influence: Humanism, rationalism, and scientific methods encouraged questioning religious issues.
Revolutionary Changes: Rise of the middle class, expansion of trade, geographical discoveries, wealth accumulation, and capitalism.

questions.text: Explain in detail the effects of the Renaissance on Europe.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain in detail the effects of the Renaissance on Europe. (D)

answer.value:
A) Growth of scientific temper: Rational and experimental scientific thinking developed in place of superstitions and blind religious beliefs.
B) Progress of regional languages: Literary works which were earlier limited to Latin came to be written in common languages like English, Italian, French, German, and Spanish, leading to the creation of excellent literature.
C) Rise of humanism: Instead of focusing on the afterlife, greater importance was given to human welfare, love, and individual freedom in this world.
D) New style in art and architecture: Painting and sculpture went beyond religious boundaries and depicted liveliness, realism, and the natural beauty of the human body.
E) Invention of the printing press: As Johannes Gutenberg invented the printing press, knowledge and new ideas spread very rapidly among common people.

questions.text: Analyze, the major effects of new geographical discoveries on world history.
questions.text_as_printed: Analyze, the major effects of new geographical discoveries on world history. (D)

answer.value:
A) Expansion of global trade: With the discovery of new lands, the Atlantic Ocean became the center of global trade. Countries like Portugal, Spain, and England emerged as very rich nations.
B) Rise of colonialism and imperialism: European nations established their colonies in Asia, Africa, and America and began to exploit the wealth of those regions.
C) Spread of slavery: The inhumane "slave trade" began, in which Africans were enslaved and transported in ships to America to work on plantations.
D) Cultural exchange: European religion, language, and culture spread to the New World. Similarly, new food items like potato, maize, tobacco, and tomatoes were introduced to Europe.
